label: rejected

evidence.V1: Silhouette reads as a grass tuft (fan of tapered blades over a mound) in front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view still reads as radiating blades.
evidence.V2: Big mound and medium blades read, but the small level is only a hard light-green tip band; blades are near-identical spikes with no secondary grouping.
evidence.V3: Blades are straight tapered prisms poking out of a dome; partly stylised curve on the two outer blades, the rest stiff.
evidence.V4: Mound edge is a low-poly polygon outline with flat facets while blades have razor tips and hard diamond cross-sections; treatment inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Close-up base shows faceted dark wedges where blades enter the mound and a stray short blade stub with a dark flat face; tip colour band is a hard step; minor artifacts.
evidence.V6: Single green hue in ~3 values (dark mound, mid blade, light tips); colourways (autumn, frost) swap cleanly.
evidence.V7: 600 tris vs small target 600 - at target.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material and green hue match, but blades are separate intersecting shells (240 cross-shell overlaps) rather than a fused smooth organic shell, and the mound is faceted.
evidence.V9: Foliage flags correct: Anchored, CanCollide/CanTouch/CanQuery off, Box fidelity, Color white, origin bottom-centre.

evidence.V1: Reads as a grass tuft on a mound in front, three-quarter, top and silhouette.
evidence.V2: Mound base, varied tall/short blades and lighter tip bands give a clear big/medium/small read.
evidence.V3: Blades are thick horn-like wedges and too few; the mound is a plain polygonal dome - only partly stylised.
evidence.V4: Blades have hard faceted edges and stepped tip bands; the mound rim is a visibly polygonal outline - inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Studio close-ups show stray faceting on blade sides, a hard colour step at blade tips and a hot spot on the dome.
evidence.V6: One green in three values (dark mound, mid blades, light tips); colourways hold the same structure.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material matches, but faceted horn-like blades do not read as the kit's smooth fused organic shells.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CanCollide/CanTouch/CanQuery off, Box fidelity, Color white, SmoothPlastic - correct foliage flags.

evidence.V1: Front, three-quarter and silhouette read as a grass tuft on a mound; top view reads as a spiky starburst over a round base.
evidence.V2: Two tiers only: the domed mound and about seven blades of similar size; no small-scale detail (short filler blades, pebbles, root tufts).
evidence.V3: Partly stylised: curved blades are fine, but the mound is oversized and dome-like relative to the sparse blades, so it reads like a pincushion.
evidence.V4: Blade edges are razor-thin with angular tips and the mound has a visibly polygonal rim; no consistent softened edge treatment.
evidence.V5: Blade close-ups show a hard horizontal colour step where the light tip band meets the blade body (reads as a seam) and visible faceting on blade sides and the mound rim.
evidence.V6: Disciplined single foliage hue in three values (dark base, mid blade, light tip); autumn and frost colourways keep the structure.
evidence.V7: 600 tris vs small target 600, at target.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material, but the kit asks organic forms as fused smooth shells; here blades are separate faceted shells stuck into a faceted dome.
evidence.V9: Foliage studio line correct: anchored, CanCollide/CanTouch/CanQuery off, white colour, origin bottom-centre; gates pass.

top_fixes: Smooth the mound (more segments or weighted normals) and blend blade bases into it instead of hard intersections
Vary blade bend/lean and add 2-3 smaller blades in clusters for a real small-scale level
Gradient the tip colour over a couple of loops instead of a hard band
Remove or rework the short stub blade
Use more, thinner, smoothly curved blades with gradient (not stepped) tip colour
Smooth/round the mound and hide its rim slightly below ground
Spread blades more evenly around the clump so the top view is not lopsided
Blend the tip colour band gradually (or bevel the band boundary) and add a few more segments to blades so they curve smoothly
Shrink and flatten the mound and add more, varied blades including short filler ones so the tuft hides the base
Smooth the base rim and fuse blade roots into the mound for the kit's fused-shell organic look
